title: Populate the adapters/ workspace root with the shared IDE adapter contract
description:
Objective: land the adapters/ workspace root and the ONE editor-neutral contract every IDE adapter implements — daemon discovery, daemon start, and control-room open — so a specific adapter can be thin and a security schedule has a declared boundary to fault-inject against. Created by governor-f70d1157 at human direction. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must plan it. What follows is measurement and constraint, not a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS. pnpm-workspace.yaml globs `adapters/*` and carries the comment "Reserved, not yet populated: external integrations". The directory has never existed. That absence is a named blocker on task-05ce9b8f (Security fault matrix), whose hard dependency is "Schedule coverage checker and all production adapters", and it leaves task-9fd52b41 (Thin JetBrains adapter) with nothing to be thin against.

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 18:58Z. Verify every line before trusting it — this description was written from greps, not by the module author.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — 4 of 5 production adapters are landed, so this is the last one:
- packages/runner/src/providers/claude and .../codex — provider adapters, both DONE
- packages/mcp/src/stdio and packages/mcp/src/http — MCP transports, both DONE
- apps/daemon/src/http — the daemon HTTP boundary, with a real listener
- `adapters/` — ABSENT. No IDE/editor adapter code exists anywhere: grep for jetbrains|vscode|IdeAdapter across packages and apps returns nothing but an unrelated control-room test.

WHAT THE ADAPTER COMPOSES, all verified present:
- apps/daemon/package.json declares bin {"moe-daemon": "./src/daemon-main.ts"} — the daemon is a startable process, so DISCOVER and START are real operations rather than aspirations.
- apps/control-room/package.json has a `build` script — there are static assets to OPEN.
- packages/control-room-client exposes a curated root surface (5 export statements) — the generated client an adapter drives rather than reimplementing.

WHAT THIS TASK LANDS — one workspace package under adapters/, editor-neutral, and nothing more:
1. The adapters/ workspace root, populated so the existing `adapters/*` glob resolves.
2. A single contract module declaring the IDE adapter boundary as TYPES and STABLE REASON CODES: discover a running daemon, start one if absent, and open the control room (embedded or browser fallback). Every operation fails closed with a stable code and the refusing layer.
3. Its consumer edge, per Clause 1: the contract must be reachable from the package root, proven by a plain-Node import probe.

NOT IN SCOPE, and this list is binding: any JetBrains-specific code (that is task-9fd52b41 and it owns adapters/jetbrains/**); VS Code or any other specific editor; duplicating product logic, canonical state or lifecycle transitions; spawning real processes or launching a real browser in tests; changing apps/daemon, apps/control-room, or packages/control-room-client; a second client implementation.

THE TRAP THIS BOARD HAS HIT REPEATEDLY: do not build a surface for data that does not exist, and do not certify anything. This task ships a BOUNDARY, not an integration and not a proof. If a DoD item asks you to demonstrate a working IDE integration, that belongs to task-9fd52b41.

WHO IS WAITING — name both as consumers per Clause 1 rather than leaving the edge implied: task-9fd52b41 (Thin JetBrains adapter) implements this contract; task-05ce9b8f (Security fault matrix) needs a declared IDE authority boundary to schedule hostile/stale/replay cases against.

Hard dependencies: none. Everything named above is committed at HEAD.

Verification: pnpm typecheck && pnpm test, plus a plain-Node import probe of the new package root recorded verbatim.

Size: if the plan exceeds 12 steps or 10 distinct affectedFiles, SPLIT it and say so rather than padding.
definitionOfDone: The adapters/ workspace root exists and resolves under the existing `adapters/*` glob in pnpm-workspace.yaml, with pnpm install succeeding and the glob's reserved comment updated or removed to reflect that it is now populated. The workspace file is shared state — change only that line.

One editor-neutral contract module declares the IDE adapter boundary: discover a running daemon, start one when absent, and open the control room with an embedded-or-browser-fallback outcome. It contains TYPES, a frozen stable reason-code vocabulary and a refusing-layer label — no editor-specific code, no process spawning, no browser launching.

Every operation's failure path is total and fails closed: a test asserts the SPECIFIC stable reason code AND the refusing layer for each failure case per epic rail 6, never merely that the operation did not succeed. The case sweep asserts it generated a non-zero number of cases so an emptied sweep cannot pass silently.

The contract is reachable from the new package's root specifier — proven by a PLAIN-NODE import probe recorded verbatim in the completion evidence, not by vitest, which resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and is structurally blind to a missing bridge.

No editor-specific identifier appears anywhere in the deliverable: a test greps the owned paths for jetbrains/vscode/intellij and asserts zero matches, so the boundary cannot quietly become one editor's adapter.
Both consumers are named in the plan per Clause 1: task-9fd52b41 (Thin JetBrains adapter) implements this contract, task-05ce9b8f (Security fault matrix) schedules against this boundary.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test exit 0, with any foreign red attributed by path per global rail 3 and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: Editor-neutral or nothing. If you find yourself writing a JetBrains, IntelliJ or VS Code identifier, stop — that is task-9fd52b41's scope and this contract exists precisely so that task can be thin.

This ships a BOUNDARY, not an integration and not a proof. Do not spawn a daemon process, do not launch a browser, do not certify that any IDE works. Ports are declared and injected; the real implementations belong to the adapter and to the fault schedules.

Read apps/daemon/package.json (the moe-daemon bin), apps/control-room/package.json (the build script) and packages/control-room-client/src/index.ts before naming a single symbol. Verify each on disk rather than copying from this description (skill: explore-before-assume) — it was written by a governor from greps.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and the refusing layer, per epic rail 4 and rail 6. An operation that cannot determine whether a daemon is running returns a typed UNKNOWN with its reason, never an optimistic success.

Do not reimplement the generated control-room client. packages/control-room-client is the seam an adapter drives; a second client will drift from the generated schema that the design requires HTTP, MCP, UI and IDE to share.
pnpm-workspace.yaml and the lockfile are shared state and three tasks contended over them today. Touch only the single glob comment line, and verify with git diff --stat before committing.
Keep each production source focused: target <=250 physical lines, split before 400.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — never git add -A. After `git add`, run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm the list is EXACTLY your owned paths: the git index is shared on this board and carries other agents' staged files. Hand QA blob shas (git hash-object <path>) alongside a base-ref diff rather than a commit sha.

implementationPlan.description: RED first (TDD). Create adapters/ide-contract/src/ide-adapter-contract.test.ts against the not-yet-written production module. Pin the boundary's three operations — DISCOVER a running daemon, START one when absent, OPEN the control room — and for each, assert the SPECIFIC stable reason code AND `layer` on every failure path, never merely that the call did not succeed (epic rail 6). Required cases: discovery that cannot determine whether a daemon runs returns a typed UNKNOWN carrying its reason, NOT an optimistic success (task rail 4); start refused; start unverified (a process was launched but listening was never confirmed — that is UNKNOWN, not success); control-room assets missing; embedded view unavailable, which must yield the browser-fallback outcome rather than a failure; browser fallback refused. Drive the sweep from the frozen exported code tuple and assert `expect(seen.size).toBe(IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES.length)` AND `expect(seen.size).toBeGreaterThan(0)` so an emptied tuple cannot pass silently (DoD 3). Every port is a plain injected object literal in the test — no child process, no browser, no network (task rail 2).
implementationPlan.note:
RED first, confirmed by running it: `pnpm test adapters/ide-contract` -> exit 1, "Error: Cannot find module './index.js' imported from .../ide-adapter-contract.test.ts". No production surface exists yet, so nothing here can be passing vacuously.

17 hand-written cases, each asserting the FULL result object with toEqual — so "did not succeed" can never satisfy one; the specific code and, on every failure, the refusing layer are both pinned (epic rail 6). Cases per operation: discovery 6, start 5, open 6.

The vocabulary the test drives against production: 14 codes, 4 layers.
  DISCOVER: DAEMON_RUNNING(OK), DAEMON_ABSENT(OK), DAEMON_STATE_UNKNOWN(UNKNOWN/DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT), DAEMON_DISCOVERY_REFUSED(REFUSED/DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT), DAEMON_ENDPOINT_MISSING(UNKNOWN/IDE_ADAPTER)
  START: DAEMON_STARTED(OK), DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED(UNKNOWN/IDE_ADAPTER), DAEMON_START_REFUSED(REFUSED/DAEMON_START_PORT)
  OPEN: CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED(OK), CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK(OK), CONTROL_ROOM_ASSETS_MISSING(REFUSED/CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT), CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_REFUSED(REFUSED/CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT), CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_UNKNOWN(UNKNOWN/IDE_ADAPTER)
  TOTALITY: EVIDENCE_MALFORMED(REFUSED/IDE_ADAPTER), exercised once per operation via a cast that reproduces the untyped value a foreign IDE runtime can hand across the boundary.

Anti-vacuity assertions, all of them hand-written rather than derived:
- CASES.length pinned to MINIMUM_CASES=17 AND >0, plus unique case names — an emptied or deduplicated sweep reddens.
- seen.size === IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES.length AND >0 AND the sorted sets are equal, where `seen` is collected from the PRODUCTION functions' actual return values, not from the expectations. This proves every declared code is producible by production code; dropping a tuple entry reddens (drill b).
- Layer is asserted to VARY: a test asserts the refusing-layer set has size > 1 and contains both IDE_ADAPTER and DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT, so a layer assertion cannot be a constant. Successes are asserted NOT to carry a layer.
- Both vocabularies asserted frozen and duplicate-free.

Task rail 2 respected: every port value is a plain injected object literal. No child process, no browser, no network anywhere in this file.

Note on the anti-optimistic-success design (task rail 4): LISTENING-without-an-endpoint and LAUNCHED_UNCONFIRMED are UNKNOWN with a reason at the IDE_ADAPTER layer — the contract refuses to trust the port's claim rather than reporting a usable daemon.

implementationPlan.description: The contract module: adapters/ide-contract/src/index.ts, plus its one-line sibling bridge index.js containing exactly `export * from "./index.ts";` (LF, matching packages/control-room-client/src/index.js byte-for-byte in form). CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT, measured from the reference probe's own comment: `--experimental-strip-types` ERASES every `export type`, so a module of pure types imports as an empty namespace and the entrypoint probe's `hasNamedExports` assertion fails. The module must therefore carry real VALUE exports: `IDE_ADAPTER_LAYER = 'IDE_ADAPTER' as const`, a frozen `IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES` tuple, and one pure decision function per operation that maps injected port evidence to a typed result. Types alone would also make step 4's tests vacuous — there would be no production surface to assert against, only a helper reimplementing the contract, which the global test rail forbids. Ports (`DaemonDiscoveryPort`, `DaemonStartPort`, `ControlRoomOpenPort`) are declared as interfaces and injected; nothing here spawns or launches. Keep it at or below 250 physical lines measured by `grep -c ''`; if the three operations do not fit, split by operation rather than growing the file.

FAIL-CLOSED AND TOTAL. Each operation ends in a `malformed(...)` return rather than trusting its input, because evidence crosses a boundary from a foreign editor runtime that does not honour these types — that is the EVIDENCE_MALFORMED code, refused at the IDE_ADAPTER layer. Anti-optimistic-success (task rail 4): LISTENING or LISTENING_CONFIRMED without a usable endpoint is DAEMON_ENDPOINT_MISSING/UNKNOWN, and LAUNCHED_UNCONFIRMED is DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN — a launched process is never reported as a started daemon. A determinate DAEMON_ABSENT is a success because it is what licenses a start; an unavailable embedded view is not a failure but the browser-fallback path (DoD 2).

Ports (DaemonDiscoveryPort, DaemonStartPort, ControlRoomOpenPort, plus IdeAdapterPorts) are declared interfaces only. Nothing in this file spawns, launches, or opens a socket (task rail 2), and no part of packages/control-room-client is reimplemented (task rail 5).

implementationPlan.description: The plain-Node import probe DoD 4 requires, as adapters/ide-contract/src/ide-adapter-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.
